messages:
Sophie Carter: @Maya quick heads-up — ACME (large enterprise) just pushed back on our reserved-capacity proposal. They want a per-token bucket that auto-buys burst capacity and a small SLA credit if we throttle them during spikes. Thoughts?
Maya Patel: hm. do we have precedent for auto-buys tied to burst? usually we separate reserved vs burst and charge overage per-token. they want smoothing + a credit floor. :thinking:
Raj Singh: can we model it as: keep reserved commit X, allow burst up to Y tokens at rate R_burst, if we slow them because of cluster constraints then apply a SLA credit = min(credit_cap, alpha * affected_tokens * per_token_rate)? need concrete numbers.
Lin Zhao: finance take: credits are basically deferred discounts. for accounting simplicity we prefer fixed overage rates + one-off credits (not recurring). if they want smoothing we could offer a small pre-purchased "burst bucket" that drains then auto-replenishes (prepay) vs pay-as-you-go.
Sophie Carter: ACME's ask: want minimal ops visibility — they want predictable invoices. Sales pushed for a blended-per-token floor and an emergency SLA credit if we intentionally degrade their traffic during business hours.
Maya Patel: operational constraints: we can set a policy that routes to lower-cost variants, but we won't proactively degrade unless capacity exhausted. I don't love open-ended credits. Suggest we offer 2 options: 1) "Blended prepaid bucket": monthly prepaid tokens used for burst at fixed blended rate; 2) "Reserved + capped overage": reserved commit + overage per-token with a 1% monthly credit cap for throttles.
Raj Singh: that matches product guardrails. For launch criteria we need: acceptance tests (billing calc matches expected invoice), SLO trigger -> credit issuance flow, clear UX in Console showing bucket usage + alarms.
Lin Zhao: need sample pricing numbers from sales. Also need to flag tax/contract impact for credits. finance requires contract clause: credits apply only for demonstrable throttling and capped at N months of charges.
BillingBot: Policy excerpt: "Credits are issued when Redwood-verified throttling > 5 minutes within a 24h window and only up to 1% of monthly invoice, unless explicitly agreed in contract."
Sophie Carter: next steps: @Raj can you add a product intake ticket with ACME as customer context, include options 1/2, required acceptance tests, and attach the billing policy snippet. Set priority to P1 if sales confirm ARR > $500k.
Raj Singh: will do. I'll create ticket and tag @Maya @Lin. linking provisional ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-3145 (draft)
Maya Patel: also add a small AB test for UX: show blended bucket vs reserved+overage in console and capture sales conversion metric.
Sophie Carter: agreed. keep customer on a short-term pilot for 3 months, measure costs and incidents. :thumbsup:
Lin Zhao: finance will draft the contract credit cap language. sending via DM to @Sophie.
Sophie Carter: thanks all — I'll summarize for ACME and send proposal tomorrow morning.
